leftEvidence.title: Liberty yields before stumbling and conscience

points.label: Knowledge and judgment
points.left: Liberty yields before stumbling and conscience. Romans 14:13–23 belongs to Gospel, Israel, and shared life.
points.right: Liberty encounters a wounded conscience. 1 Corinthians 8:7–13 belongs to Corinth and contested apostleship.

points.label: Effect on another person
points.left: Liberty yields before stumbling and conscience. Therefore let’s not judge one another any more, but judge this rather, that no man put a stumbling block in his brother’s way, or an occasion for falling. But he who doubts is condemned if he eats, because it isn’t of faith; and whatever is not of faith is sin.
points.right: Liberty encounters a wounded conscience. However, that knowledge isn’t in all men. But some, with consciousness of an idol until now, eat as of a thing sacrificed to an idol, and their conscience, being weak, is defiled. Therefore, if food causes my brother to stumble, I will eat no meat forever more, that I don’t cause my brother to stumble.

payload.tension: Food, conscience, and another person places two independently valuable sources together while preserving their distinct audience, form, sequence, and stated purpose.
